text:
sara: Quick experiment — rolling out topology-aware spot mix in us-west2 for the next 3h. Goal: bias capacity-optimized for P4/P4x-like SKUs in AZs with steady supply and keep price-optimized lanes for A40 bursts. Anyone see network egress or cross-AZ constraints? :thinking:

devin: +1. couple notes: tune graceful-drain to 90s for preemptible nodes to reduce mid-request terminations. set `eviction_grace_period=90` on the nodegroup policy.

marco: Also add nodeAffinity label `spot-preference=capacity` so scheduler prefers those nodes for long-running model shards and KV cache priming.

ashley: Can we run a 2h canary at 10% traffic? Metrics to watch: p95 latency, CPU steal, eviction rate per AZ, and egress bytes per-minute.

sara: yes — canary scheduled. sample autoscaler placement snippet:```yaml
autoscaler:
  policy: topology-aware
  weights:
    p4: 0.7
    a40: 0.3
  eviction_grace_period: 90
  drain_timeout: 120
  fallback: nearest-price
```

sara: quick k8s tip: `kubectl label nodes gpu-usw2-1 spot-preference=capacity --overwrite` and use `pod.spec.affinity.nodeAffinity` for long-running replicas.

ops-bot: [alert] preemptible-eviction spike in us-west2-b — 5 nodes evicted in last 60s. https://metrics/evictions?ts=2712345100 :warning:

devin: good catch. plan: if spike persists, autoscaler fallback to price-optimized pool in same AZ via `fallback: nearest-price` and throttle new shard placements for 5m. Also enable soft-evict log level to capture in-flight token failures.

marco: another thought — cap cross-AZ egress when spilling to fallback pool. Add `max_egress_per_hour` in placement policy to avoid surprise costs.

ashley: observability checklist: tag traces with `placement.policy`, `start_pool`, `fallback_pool` so we can correlate evictions -> model errors quickly. Add a short eval set to detect quality regressions from pool switching.

sara: ok rolling now, canary id=canary-38. capturing logs to s3://infra-playbacks/topo-canary-38/. Ping here immediately if you see increased 5xx or token truncation.
